18. I have carefully gone through the charges levelled against the accused and also the evidence relied by the prosecution.

19. In the decision reported in (2017) 11 SCC 195- Yogesh Singh Vs Mahabeer Singh and others ..At para 15 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"15.
It is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that the guilt of the accused must be proved beyond all reasonable doubts.
However, the burden on the prosecution is only to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubt and not all doubts".

Here, it is worthwhile to reproduce the observations made by Venkatachaliah, ., in State of U.P. Vs.
Krishna Gopal and Anr., (1988) 4 SCC 302:
"25. ...
Doubts would be called reasonable if they are free from a zest for abstract speculation.
Law cannot afford any favorite other than truth.
To constitute reasonable doubt, it must be free from an overemotional response.
Doubts must be actual and substantial doubts as to the guilt of the accused person arising from the evidence, or from the lack of it, as opposed to mere vague apprehensions.
A reasonable doubt is not an imaginary, trivial or a merely possible doubt; but a fair doubt based upon reason and common sense.
It must grow out of the evidence in the case".
Keeping the requirement of the above said provisions of law and law laid down in the above said decision in my mind I have carefully examined the evidence placed on record.
This court noticed that P.W.1 to 4 who are examined in support of the case of prosecution are all interested witnesses.
The evidence of these witnesses is to be scrutinized cautiously.
No independent eye witness has been cited in the charge sheet.
Further more the prosecution has not examined any independent witnesses in support of its case.
Therefore, there is no independent corroboration to the case of prosecution.
There is no information as to who is the owner of the godown where the accused illegally possessed/stored 54 gas cylinders.
The C.W.1 has not furnished any photo or documentary evidence to show that the accused was at the alleged place of incident when he conducted raid.
PW1 has not recorded the statement of adjoining building.
21. It is the burden of the prosecution to show that they have seized the alleged goods from the possession of the accused in the presence of pancha witnesses under seizure mahazar.
To prove the facts of the evidence the complainant and also the pancha witnesses are very essential.

22. On perusal of the evidence adduced by the prosecution in support of their case, as already stated above the Seizure Mahazar Witness has not been examined, so it clearly reveals that the Mahazar is not proved beyond all reasonable doubt.
23. There are no independent witnesses to the case of prosecution.
Although the place of incident is a town, no independent witnesses are cited as the witnesses.
The evidence of PW-1 to 4 is not corroborative to each other.
24. In the absence of corroborative evidence, the contents of exhibits are also not sufficient to prove the case of prosecution beyond reasonable doubts.
Further there is no corroboration in the evidence of the official witnesses also.
25. Looking to the weak type of evidence, there are two possibilities, one pointing towards the guilt of accused and another pointing towards the innocence of the accused.

Therefore, looking to the entire material on record, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the alleged offences.

26. On careful appreciation of evidence led on behalf of prosecution, it reveals that, none of the witnesses have spoken to with regard to essential ingredients constituting the offence of refilling small cylinders and regarding the offence
No material has been seized by the IO to show that the accused was selling the refilled small gas cylinders or refilling gas to small cylinders as alleged in the complaint.

Hence, on careful and meticulous appreciation of evidence and considering the totality of circumstances, the prosecution has failed to prove beyond all reasonable doubt that,
the charges leveled against the accused.
Further in this particular case, the defence of the accused is that, the police have falsely implicated the accused in order to show statistic to the state.
When the prosecution has not proved the seizure mahazar with independent evidence, the evidence of other officials is formal in nature.
In the absence of corroborative evidence, only on the basis of the official witnesses, this court cannot come to the conclusion that the accused committed the offence as alleged by the Prosecution.
When the Prosecution has not proved its case, beyond all reasonable doubt, it creates doubt in the mind of this court.
Hence, the accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt and he is entitled for acquittal.
